pronunciation.approximation: Say "nafanua" with the stress and length implied by the scholarly restoration "Nafanua".
pronunciation.note: The ASCII form "nafanua" is a DNS compromise; the restoration "Nafanua" preserves the name's scholarly dignity.

domains.title: Nafanua
domains.subtitle: War
domains.lead: Nafanua is war, prophecy, salvation. The name means "Hidden in the earth" and belongs to the polynesian tradition.

cards.name: Sacred Name
cards.desc: The restoration Nafanua returns the figure to scholarly recognition.

cards.name: Living Tradition
cards.desc: Honored in polynesian myth, cult, and cultural memory.

cards.name: Unicode Restoration
cards.desc: Preserved as a flagship temple despite the unregistrable plain-ASCII form.

symbols.name: Name
symbols.meaning: The restored form Nafanua, carrying scholarly and cultural weight.

mythology.lead: The stories of Nafanua place war, prophecy, salvation at the center of a living mythological world.

myths.title: Origins
myths.text: Nafanua appears in polynesian tradition as war, prophecy, salvation. The name's meaning, "Hidden in the earth", shapes the narratives told about this figure.

myths.title: Worship and Memory
myths.text: Devotees and later tradition-keepers preserved Nafanua in ritual, text, and iconography, ensuring the name survived into the modern scholarly record.

lore.culturalLegacy: Nafanua remains a touchstone for understanding polynesian religion, art, and identity.
scholarlySources: Craig, Robert D., Dictionary of Polynesian Mythology (1989).
Orbell, Margaret, A Concise Encyclopedia of Māori Myth and Legend (1998).
